feature: One color picker, everywhere a color is chosen
summary: Every swatch in the app now opens the same designed picker, including the four rows that used to raise the system color panel. It has a saturation and brightness square, HSL, RGB and HEX with a slider and a number per channel, one swatch row that switches between shades of this color, its relatives, the colors this document already uses and the ones you picked recently, a live contrast reading, an eyedropper and Save style.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. "One color picker, everywhere a color is chosen" is on by default. Save style needs the styles switch, which is also on by default.

try.do: Draw two rectangles, click one, and click the Fill swatch in the Color section.
Drag inside the square, then let go. Watch the shape repaint once, on release.
Click RGB, then HEX, and paste rgb(124, 77, 255) into the field.
Click Document in the swatch row, then click one of the colors it lists.
Turn Enable Shadow on in the Shadow section and click the swatch beside Blur.
Click the eyedropper and sample something outside the app.
Click Save style, type Brand, press Return, and look at the Library.
Press Command Z once and check the shape goes back in one step.

evaluate: Opening on Fill and then on Shadow, does it feel like the same control turning up twice, or like two controls that happen to look alike?
Is the before and after pair at the top telling you anything, or is it two swatches you never look at?
When you want a slightly darker version of what you have, is the Shades row where your hand goes, or do you still reach for the L slider?
The contrast reading says how the color does on white. Is white the background you are actually asking about?
In HSL and RGB there is no hex anywhere on screen. Did you go looking for it?
rough: The color lands on release, not while you drag, so the shape does not repaint live under the picker. That is on purpose for now: every live tick would be its own undo step, and coalescing them is a change to how edits are recorded rather than to the picker. Filed as a follow-up.

The eyedropper is the system sampler. Its own magnified loupe follows the pointer and is what shows the color live; the picker's own swatch only updates when the click lands. Building our own sampler would mean a full screen overlay and a second capture permission for a loupe macOS already draws.

Changed from the mock: the swatch row has a fourth scope, Recent. The mock has three, and dropping recents would have been a regression for the commonest move, reusing the color you just used somewhere else.

Changed from the mock: the contrast reading is fixed on white rather than switching to whichever background scores better. A readout that silently changes its own background cannot answer "can I put this on the page". The figure for black is in the tooltip.
Not built, on purpose: the Solid, Linear, Radial and Angular tabs. Three of the four would have done nothing. Gradients are a follow-up and the tab row arrives with them.

The opacity slider only appears where the thing being painted can actually keep a transparency: a shape's fill, outline, text and border, the tool color, and the measurement chip. The shadow row has its own Opacity slider a few lines below, so the picker is not given a second one to fight with it.
Screenshots are real captures of the running probe, not offscreen renders.
